review_notes:
I read the whole file and looked for repeated nontrivial reasoning. I did not open any related source files, so the judgement rests on the target file alone.

Candidates I rejected:
- `wIso` writes out `(Paths.of _).map (Sum.inr ⟨w, hw⟩)`, which is the body of `ψ₂`. This is one line of routine unfolding, so it is not worth a shared lemma.
- `uniq` and `morphismProperty_eq_top` both work with `Paths (LocQuiver W)` and `Quotient.functor`. `uniq` uses `Paths.ext_functor`, while `morphismProperty_eq_top` does an induction on paths. The two arguments are different, so there is no common block to extract.
- `WhiskeringLeftEquivalence.inverse` has `map_id` and `map_comp`, which both go through `natTrans_hcomp_injective`, `ext X` and a `simp only` call. They are short and their simp sets differ, so extracting a helper would not clearly help.
- `unitIso` and `counitIso` have different structures and use different tools.

No repeated block is substantial enough to justify a shared lemma under this rubric.
